## Reading: descriptions are absent from both tools

Tree: objectstack `f02f4f63` (origin/main), `examples/app-crm` booted with `pnpm dev:crm -- --fresh`, HTTP MCP at `/api/v1/mcp`, signed in as the seeded admin. Read at 2026-11-17T10:17Z.

| Call | Answer shape | `description` key anywhere |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `list_objects` | 7 objects, each `name`, `label`, `fieldCount` (tool text 691 bytes) | 0 hits |
| `describe_object` `crm_account` | top keys `name, label, fields, validations, enableFeatures`; 12 fields, each `name, type, label, required, readonly, system` (tool text 2738 bytes) | 0 hits |

Control, same caller, same boot: `GET /api/v1/meta/object/crm_account` serves the object `description` ("A company that the org sells to or supports.") and a `description` on 9 fields, e.g. `owner_id` ("Record owner (auto-stamped to the creating user on insert; reassignable). ...") and the other platform-injected columns (`created_at`, `updated_by`, `queue`, ...). So the text is authored and served to this caller on the `/meta` door, and neither MCP tool returns it.

Source agrees on both transports: `list_objects` projects `name/label/fieldCount` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` `listObjectSummaries`; `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts` `listObjects`), and `describe_object` projects an explicit key list with no `description` (`describeServedObject` in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` and its twin in `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`).

Side reading: no hand-authored app-crm field carries a `description` today (the 9 above are registry-injected columns); app-crm objects do.

Field-level security: both tools already read the object as the caller is served it (ADR-0106 D5), so an unreadable field is removed whole, its description with it. The ADR-0106 projection keeps `description` on the object and on readable fields as prose (`packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts`, `description: keep`), which is what the `/meta` door serves the same caller.

Next: the authorised build half (existing `description` only, no new key), with a byte cost and pins on both transports.
